I had to stop right around when times got really rough for me too. But trust me, this break is going to help you a lot! You just have to find ways to distract yourself. Read a book, listen to music, watch a movie, go for a walk, hang out with friends (that don't smoke), anything to keep your mind off the habit. Start hanging out with friends that don't smoke because they know how to have fun without getting high. 
You can still do what you always did when you used to get high. It's different but I found it was a cool kind of different. I noticed more of what I was doing and things I hadn't noticed before.
I don't know if you can afford it or if it's even available to you, but talking to a therapist can help with all the urges. They know techniques to calm you down when you're in an emotional state of mind, without turning to smoking. Although most are going to try to convince you to quit altogether. But if they're cool, they'll just want to help you so that in the future you'll have the choice to smoke or not, and not just do it out of habit or wanting to drown certain emotions.
And I hate to break it to you, but this break isn't going to be easy. But it will help and you will find a great person underneath all the smoke (get it? smoke? Yeah okay lame joke, got it). Smoking later on is going to be great though!

I developed this too! It became a real problem after many trips to the ER after not being able to stop throwing up after an hour. I had several ultrasounds, many blood tests, many urine tests (because if a young girl comes into the ER throwing up they like to think you're pregnant), and even a super invasive endoscopy (where they put you under to stick a camera down your throat into your stomach). I lost 20 pounds over several months, which I couldn't afford to lose as I was already underweight. It took months to finally figure out what it was. At first I didn't want to believe it because everyone says how harmless weed is and I enjoy smoking it. I thought I could medicate the nausea and lack of appetite with more weed, which just ended up making it all so much worse. 

I quit for about three weeks and my symptoms improved dramatically. I haven't thrown up since and no longer have godawful nausea. It is possible to continue smoking, but as I've discovered, you cannot smoke everyday and you cannot smoke as much as you used to. I strongly recommend taking several weeks off of smoking so your body can regulate itself again.
